messages.text: How do changes in automotive radar technology affect the measurement capability required from Signaling / Non-signaling Tester?

The knowledge base gave no answer: the RS Knowledge tool returned insufficient evidence for this question, so I can’t cite the corpus.

Not from the knowledge base — general engineering view:

Changes in automotive radar push “signaling / non-signaling tester” capability mainly toward wider bandwidth, higher frequency, coherent multi-channel operation, and more realistic OTA/scenario simulation.

| Automotive radar change | Measurement capability required |
|---|---|
| Shift from 24 GHz to 76–81 GHz radar | Test equipment must cover 77/79 GHz bands directly or through calibrated mmWave converters. |
| Wider FMCW bandwidths, up to several GHz | Analyzer/generator bandwidth must support large instantaneous bandwidth for range resolution and chirp linearity checks. |
| Higher range and velocity resolution | Testers need accurate frequency, phase, timing, Doppler, and low phase-noise performance. |
| MIMO and imaging radar with many TX/RX channels | Multi-channel phase-coherent generation/analysis becomes important for angle-of-arrival, beamforming, and virtual array validation. |
| More complex radar waveforms and chirp sequences | Non-signaling testers must generate and analyze arbitrary FMCW ramps, fast chirps, burst timing, modulation quality, and waveform deviations. |
| OTA validation replacing only conducted tests | Chambers, compact antenna test ranges, radar target simulators, and calibrated propagation paths are needed. |
| ADAS/AD sensor-fusion scenarios | Test setups must simulate multiple moving targets, different ranges, radar cross sections, velocities, angles, and sometimes interference. |
| Radar interference and coexistence concerns | Testers need ability to inject or analyze interference, assess susceptibility, detect ghost targets, and evaluate mitigation algorithms. |
| Production cost pressure | Non-signaling test must be fast, repeatable, automated, and able to verify frequency, power, chirp slope, bandwidth, leakage, EIRP, and receiver sensitivity quickly. |
| Functional safety expectations | Measurement systems need traceability, repeatability, scenario coverage, and failure-mode verification. |

In short: older radar testing could focus on basic RF power/frequency and simple FMCW checks. New automotive radar requires mmWave, wideband, low-phase-noise, phase-coherent, multi-channel, OTA-capable, scenario-based measurement systems. For non-signaling production test, speed and calibration are critical; for R&D and validation, realistic target and interference simulation become equally important.
